items.stem: Five changes occuring in boys and girls during adolescence are _____, _____, _____, _____ and _____.
items.answer: (1) an overall growth in body size, in which the long bones, the vertebrae and limbs grow and the adolescent gains height; (2) a spurt in muscle mass, whose peak of growth is typically around the age of 14 to 16 years; (3) growth and maturity of the reproductive organs, since in males, testes grow in size and start producing sperms and in females, the eggs or ova present in the ovary since birth begins to mature; (4) development of secondary sexual characteristics in both girls and boys, so that breasts begin to develop in girls due to the release of estrogen hormone and changes in voice are quite noticeable among boys; (5) psychosocial changes, that is changes in thoughts, mood, attractions and friendships, which accompany the physical changes.

items.stem: What are the health and educational implications of adolescent pregnancy?
items.answer: An adolescent is capable of reproduction, but reproductive maturity is reached only when a teenager is fully developed physically and physiologically, so if pregnancy occurs before reaching complete reproductive maturity, girls may risk their own health and that of the fetus. Health implications: an adolescent mother is not mentally prepared for motherhood; she is likely to be anemic; she is more prone towards maternal death while giving birth; there is likelihood of developing complications during giving birth and the reproductive tract may be damaged during childbirth; infant death are more among teenage mothers, and the baby born from teenage mother requires greater care which the teenage mother may not be able to give. Educational implications: early pregnancy and motherhood delays development of education and career of adolescent mother. There may also be economic problems and problems due to psychological immaturity of the adolescent mother, which may hamper proper care of the infant.

items.stem: Write down the process of the - (i) mid-arm circumference. (ii) measurement of height. (iii) body mass index. (iv) tongue examination. (v) examination the nail beds.
items.answer: (i) Mid-arm circumference: biceps is the muscle of mid arm, so place the beginning of the tape in the middle of the biceps, midway between shoulder and elbow joint, take the reading and record it. (ii) Measurement of height: you need only an inch tape for this; take your own height at intervals as you grow, remembering that your height at age 19 is almost the maximum height that you shall attain. (iii) Body mass index: divide your weight by square of your height, measuring weight in kg and height in meters; normal BMI range is 18 to 25, overweight is more than 25 and less then 29, and obese is more than 30. (iv) Tongue examination: note the colour, which is pink red on both upper and lower surface, the texture, which is rough on upper surface due to presence of papillae or taste buds, and the size, for if not swollen, tongue will fit comfortably inside the mouth; make tip of tongue touch roof of mouth to inspect ventral surface, and when protruded out, colour and texture can be noted for any deviation. (v) Examination of the nail beds: nail bed also needs direct physical examination, in which nail plate surface discolouration, abnormal cuticle, nail fold or nail shape require inspection, and loss of nails and lesions around nails need medical attention.

items.stem: Write a short note on pharmacology.
items.answer: Pharmacology deals with biological effects of drugs. Drugs are chemical substances used for healing, curing diseases, slowing them or preventing diseases. Their therapeutic desired actions for cure include stimulating or inhibited cell function, blocking biochemical of tissues, anti histamicric (anti allergic) action and laxative action. Drugs also have unwanted effects: side effects such as dry mouth or dangerous effects on tissues, while damage or toxicity or excessive bleeding are some effects of drugs used as medicine. Unusual responses are reasons for harmful effects of drugs, as are medication error or overdose; therefore one should never buy medicines over the counter (OTC) without a prescription with dosage and instruction written.
